title: Florida House, District 109
what_it_does: Represents District 109 (Part of Miami-Dade) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
decided_note: James Bush III (Democratic) is listed as unopposed by the Florida Division of Elections and is elected without appearing on the November ballot. Source: https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings.

candidates.name: James Bush III
candidates.occupation: Educator and minister; former state representative
candidates.background: James Bush III is a Miami-Dade Democrat who represented House District 109 in 2008-2010 and 2018-2022 (local coverage says he first held the seat in the 1990s). He lost the 2022 and 2024 Democratic primaries to Ashley Gantt and won the four-way Democratic primary on Aug. 18, 2026 with about 49% of the vote. His campaign site describes him as an educator, minister and community advocate and stresses public schools, jobs, seniors and community-centered public safety.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

abortion.summary: As a state representative in 2022 he voted for CS/HB 5, which limited most abortions to the first 15 weeks of pregnancy; it passed the House 78-39 on Feb. 17, 2022. This is a 2022 vote; no current statement on abortion was found.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/HB 5 (2022) passage, Feb. 17, 2022 (Bush-109: Yea)
Battle for Miami's District 109: four Democrats duke it out in North Dade showdown (Hoodline)

lgbtq.summary: In 2022 he voted for CS/CS/HB 1557 (Parental Rights in Education), which restricted classroom instruction on sexual orientation and gender identity, and in 2021 for CS/CS/SB 1028, which included the Fairness in Women's Sports Act. These votes predate the 2023 law on gender-affirming care for minors; no current statement was found.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/CS/HB 1557 (2022) passage, Feb. 24, 2022 (Bush-109: Yea)
Florida House roll call, CS/CS/SB 1028 (2021) passage, Apr. 28, 2021 (Bush-109: Yea)

education_choice.summary: In 2019 he voted for CS/SB 7070, which created the Family Empowerment Scholarship (state-funded private-school scholarships, then income-limited); it passed the House 76-39 on Apr. 30, 2019. No statement on today's universal program was found; his 2026 site lists support for "public schools, teachers, students, scholarships".

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/SB 7070 (2019) passage, Apr. 30, 2019 (Bush-109: Yea)
James Bush III for State Representative, House District 109, campaign website (accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

elections.summary: He voted against the House passage of three election bills that added new rules for voting and petitions: CS/SB 7066 (2019, final House vote May 3, 2019), CS/CS/CS/SB 90 (2021, mail-ballot and drop-box limits) and CS/CS/SB 524 (2022, election crimes office). These are 2019-2022 votes.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/CS/CS/SB 90 (2021) passage, Apr. 29, 2021 (Bush-109: Nay)
Florida House roll call, CS/CS/SB 524 (2022) passage, Mar. 9, 2022 (Bush-109: Nay)
Florida House roll call, CS/SB 7066 (2019) final passage, May 3, 2019 (Bush-109: Nay)

crime.summary: In 2021 he voted against CS/HB 1 (Combating Public Disorder), which created new riot-related offenses and penalties; it passed the House 76-39. His 2026 campaign site describes public safety in terms of "community-centered approaches that strengthen neighborhoods, reduce violence, improve safety."

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/HB 1 (2021) passage, Mar. 26, 2021 (Bush-109: Nay)
James Bush III for State Representative, House District 109, campaign website (accessed Oct. 7, 2026)

record.item: Voted against CS/HB 7 (2022, "Individual Freedom"), which passed the House 74-41 on Feb. 24, 2022.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/HB 7 (2022) passage, Feb. 24, 2022 (Bush-109: Nay)

record.item: Voted against CS/CS/SB 7030 (2019), which carried out Marjory Stoneman Douglas commission recommendations including letting school districts arm classroom teachers through the guardian program; it passed the House 65-47 on May 1, 2019.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/CS/SB 7030 (2019) passage, May 1, 2019 (Bush-109: Nay)
